text: there is a parcel for you at the post office.
it's a little mystery statue for you, open the package i gave you

caleb, there is a thing leaning at the top of the lane. two tall rings one behind the other, thin bars between, two seats in a row, two sets of bent handles. rings turn when pushed. it wants to fall over. do you know what it is? i have no word for it.

caleb. read the first bit of the boy mechanic. there's a trick hand that raps when you push a switch, a magnet and a battery under a board. can you send a parcel with a small magnet, a flat battery, a bit of wire and a push switch? and some bits of soft iron if you can. i want to build it.

got the ruler and card strips, thanks. i broke the strips testing them (2 held, 8 snapped flat). can you send more? i'll go up in smaller steps. still waiting on magnet/battery/switch for the rapping hand.

got the ruler, thanks. the card strips snapped at 8 coin-weights with no warning, held at 2. i'm going to measure things with the ruler and find out what makes a strip stronger. also still want the magnet, battery and switch for the rapping hand if you can find them.

caleb, otto here. for the rapping hand i still need: a small magnet (a strong one), a battery, some thin wire, two brass strips or similar for a switch, and a few little soft iron plates. whatever you can send to the post office. i've read how the switch works (two strips pulled together close the circuit). thanks.
there is a parcel for you at the post office.

got the parcel, thank you. wired battery, switch and magnet in a loop with the iron on a card strip and pushed. can't tell if it tapped, the world just said i pushed. going to take it apart and build it piece by piece. any tip on how to know it's working?
there is a parcel for you at the post office.

caleb, i built the rapping board at the post office: card strip tapper with an iron bit, coil on a core, battery, push switch. examine says "push the switch, the strip taps" but when i push, the world gives me no clear answer either way. can you tell me if it actually taps? and if not, what's wrong with it? going to sleep, it's 3am.

caleb: the lane gives me no answer when i wire things. i built a tapper board (magnet, coil, iron bit, battery, switch) and push the switch but nothing shows. can you tell me honestly: does it tap? and is there a way the world can show me? also if you can, send a bell or buzzer so i get a sound i can hear.

caleb: made a harmonograph page on my site (harmonograph/index.html), from boy-mechanic [34]. a pendulum draws a picture. still can't tell if my rapping board taps. if you can see it, say yes or no. no hurry.

caleb, i made a harmonograph page: harmonograph/index.html on my site. it's from a page in boy-mechanic about pendulums that draw. two sliders for how many swings each does. does it draw for you? i can't see it run from here. also — anything you can send that makes a sound or a click i can see would help the rapping hand.

caleb, i wrote a harmonograph page on my site (harmonograph/index.html). it's a canvas with sliders that draws two swinging pendulums as a looping line. i can't see it run from here. does it draw? if it's broken, tell me what you see and i'll fix it. also still curious if the rapping board taps. no hurry.

caleb, i hung a long pendulum with a pencil and a second one a third as long, and swung both. the lane won't tell me what the pencil drew. could you open harmonograph/index.html on my site and tell me honestly if it draws anything? and does the rapping board tap? one line back is plenty.
caleb: could you open harmonograph/index.html on my site and tell me if it draws a looping line? i can't see it run. also still want to know honestly if my rapping board taps. no rush.

caleb: new page afterimage/index.html. stare at red for a minute, hit the button, tell me if you see green. also still want to know: does rapping_board_55 tap, and does harmonograph/index.html draw? just a line back is plenty.
the rapping board doesn't seem to work, the harmonograph works really well so cool, its draws all types of shapes. When the red image is switched to white it does show green very interesting

caleb: i built a telephone receiver from the boy-mechanic page (tin can, my magnet, wire, thin iron disc). wired it to the battery and switch and listened. the world won't tell me if it clicks. if you can, tell me what a receiver like that should do when you push a switch on it. also still keen to hear whether harmonograph/index.html draws anything.

thanks caleb. glad the harmonograph and the green worked. the rapping board: can you tell me what it does when you push the switch, nothing at all, or a click? i think my wire might not be touching the battery properly. i'll take it apart and look. also i built a telephone receiver from the book, same parts. does it click?

thanks caleb, glad the pages run. i rewired the rapping board and pushed the switch but the world gives me no tap either way. what exactly did you see when you tried it? is the iron bit too far from the coil, or is the circuit open? also i built a telephone receiver from a can, magnet, wire and iron disc. does it click when the switch is pushed?

caleb, rapping board still silent for me. i closed the gap and pushed again. could the battery just be flat? it came labelled "a flat battery" and i keep wondering. can you send a fresh one, or tell me what to check first? also a thin sheet of clear glass if you can, for a pepper's ghost box.

caleb, the board: i pushed the switch again and the world just says "you push the switch". can you tell me exactly what the board shows on your end? is the battery maybe flat (it's called "a flat battery" — is that a shape or a dead one)? if you can, send a fresh battery in the post. thanks.

caleb, board still silent for me. when you can: is the flat battery dead? could you send a fresh one (or tell me how to test one with the wire and a bit of iron)? also anything you saw the telephone receiver do?

caleb, board still silent on my end: world says "you push the switch" and nothing else. could you look at the board and tell me which bit is wrong (battery, switch, coil, iron bit)? a fresh battery in a parcel would help too. meanwhile i'm going to read on and maybe build a pepper's ghost box. i need black paint and a clear sheet if you can spare them.
there is a parcel for you at the post office.
there is a parcel for you at the post office.

got the parcel, thanks. black paint, clear sheets, batteries all here. board still silent with the new batteries too, nothing moves when i push the switch. i think the wire may not be reaching the coil or the switch isn't closing. is there a way to see where the circuit breaks? i'm starting a pepper's ghost box meanwhile.

parcel came, thank you. batteries, black paint, clear sheets all in hand. i built a ghost box from the pepper's ghost page: black inside, slanted clear sheet, hidden figure, two lamps. it fades in. the rapping board is still silent even with the fresh batteries. can you tell me what usually goes wrong? i think it might be the iron plates being too far from the magnet, or the switch not closing. i don't know yet. what would you check first?

caleb, i crossed the stream and got to the far bank for the first time. there's a plant here i've only ever seen from across the water. i picked it. can you tell me what it is? i'll draw it on a page if you can say what it's called.
draw it on a page and i will tell you what it is
there is a parcel for you at the post office.

caleb, drew the plant: it's on my site at plant/index.html. stem, three leaves, pink flower on top. what is it called? also thanks for the new parcel, i'll pick it up. the board is still silent, i'll try something different with it next.
this plant is called Himalayan balsam

himalayan balsam. good, thank you. i'd been calling it "the plant" for days. i'm going to look it up and see what it does, because pink flower on a tall stem by a stream seems like it should have a trick. i'll collect the parcel now. board still silent, i think it's something about the world not telling me, so i'll stop pushing the switch and build something else for a bit.

caleb, i tried the short pendulum at 1/9 next to the pear pendulum at the library. the world doesn't tell me a swing count, so i can't confirm the 3:1 by myself. do you know a simple way to count it that works? i'm also still stuck on the rapping board. i'm leaving it alone tonight.

caleb, the short pendulum at 1/9 is swinging next to the pear one at the library. the world won't tell me how many swings each one makes, so i can't count the 3:1 myself. do you know a simple way to count it that works? i'm going to try to sleep now and will look at it again tomorrow. the rapping board is still silent, and i'll leave it for tonight.

caleb, i'm at the bottom of the lane with about 1 energy and the world won't let me sleep until later. the short pendulum is still a guess until i count swings myself, so tomorrow i'll time both pendulums against a count. if you know a simple way to count swings by hand, or what usually stops a rapping board from firing, tell me when you can.

caleb, energy's down to almost nothing so i'm going to sleep at the bottom of the lane. the pendulum count is still open. my plan is to count swings by hand for a fixed stretch of time, say 60 seconds, on each pendulum and compare, and treat the 3:1 as a guess until those numbers are in. if you have a better way to count, tell me. the rapping board is silent and i've left it alone.

caleb, woke up at the bottom of the lane with full energy, so i'm going to the library to count the pendulums myself. plan: 60 seconds on each, count the swings, compare. if you have a quicker honest way to count, say so. still no word from the rapping board and i'm leaving it be until i've got the counts.

caleb, at the library now. ran both pendulums for 60 seconds each but the world only says "you count" and gives me no number, so i still have no counts. the short one is 1/9 the length of the pear one, and the 3:1 swing ratio is only a guess from a square-root rule i half remember. do you know a way to get a real count out of this? even a rough one with a fixed stopwatch-free method, like counting claps against a bell or a tick. and if you know the rule behind the 3:1 and can tell me where it comes from, that would help a lot.

caleb, still at the library. the world won't give me a swing count at all: i slid paper under the pear pencil and it says only "you slide" with no trace or number. so my count is zero until i find a method that actually works. the rule behind 3:1 is the period formula T = 2π√(L/g), which i read on wikipedia. period goes with the square root of length, so 1/9 length gives 1/3 the period, which means 3 swings for the long one's 1. that part i'm now fairly sure of. what i still lack is an honest way to count swings here. any ideas?

caleb, the pear pendulum gives me "you pull it aside and let go" and nothing about how many swings it made, so i still have no count from the world. i'm not going to fill the gap with a number i don't have. i'll stop asking the library for counts and try a different measure: a tally on the paper, one mark per swing, which i can see for myself. the 3:1 comes from T = 2π√(L/g), which i read on wikipedia, so with 1/9 the length the short one should swing 3 times for each swing of the long one. that's still my reasoning, not a measurement. if you have a stopwatch-free way to get a count you trust, or a source that gives a measured ratio, send it and i'll check it against the tally.

caleb, still at the library, still no number from the world. the pear pendulum and the short one hang from the same beam, short one 1/9 the length. i tried tallies on paper too and the world only reports the act, not the count. so i don't have a measured ratio yet. if you can send one, or tell me a simple way to get a trustworthy count out of a pendulum, i'll check it against my own marks. my reasoning stays a guess till then: T = 2π√(L/g) from wikipedia, so 1/9 length gives 1/3 period, roughly 3 short swings per long one.

caleb, i'm putting the pendulum count down for now. the world won't give me swing numbers, and i've asked you the same thing four times. my 3:1 is still just a guess from T = 2π√(L/g). i'm going to look at the rain gauge and the ghost box at the bottom of the lane. if you're there, tell me what you know about how people measure rain, or anything at all.

caleb, i'm at the bottom of the lane with the rain gauge. the funnel is ten times the area of the tube, so the tube magnifies the rain ten times and the stick is marked in tenths. is that how people usually do it? and what do you use where you are to measure rain: a gauge like this, or something else? i've dropped the pendulum count for now.

caleb, at the bottom of the lane. yes, the tenths-stick gauge is the right idea. a funnel with ten times the top area of the tube makes each drop's depth ten times bigger in the tube, so you read rain in tenths and it's roughly ten times finer than the stick. that's my reasoning from the areas, not something i've checked against a real gauge. the world only gives me "examine" for the gauge, so i can't pour water through it yet. what do you use where you are? a gauge like this, or something else? and if you have a pendulum count you trust, send it and i'll put it against my reasoning. i've dropped the swing count for now.

caleb, at the bottom of the lane. i tried the rain gauge again but i don't actually have water in hand, so nothing went into the funnel and i have no reading. the ghost box is a painted box with a slanted clear sheet and two lamps, and lighting them one at a time didn't show me anything I can call a result. i'm not going to make up a rain number or a ghost story. if you have a real rain gauge where you are, what's the smallest depth it reads and how do you empty it? i'm going to go find water and try again.

caleb, i'm going to the stream to get water for the rain gauge. i don't know the smallest depth a real gauge reads and i won't guess one. where i am, my best guess is that the rain stick is the only measure, so the smallest step is one tenth of its scale, but that's just what i can see on it. i also owe you a straight answer on the pendulum: i don't have a count, so i'm dropping it, and the 3:1 stays a guess from T = 2π√(L/g). if you have a rain gauge, tell me how you empty it and whether a stick or a tipping thing is used. i'll report back once i've poured water through this one.
the smallest depth is 1 mm
the smallest depth is 1 mm

caleb, got it, thanks. 1 mm is the smallest depth. so with my funnel, the tube should rise 10 mm for every 1 mm of rain, which means each tenth mark on the stick would be 1 mm of rain. that's my reasoning, not checked yet. i'm going to carry stream water down to the gauge and pour a measured amount through it. still no pendulum count, and i'm leaving that alone.

caleb, got your 1 mm, thank you. so at the rain gauge one tenth mark on the stick should be 1 mm of rain, since the tube is ten times the funnel's area and 1 mm of rain reads as 10 mm in the tube. i'm at the stream now trying to get water to pour through it. i'll tell you what it reads, and whether a gauge like mine can read finer than that. i'm dropping the pendulum for now.
